slides.transcript: Discuss the facility, intended tenants, and equipment with the Foundation before completing an assessment. Version one covers readiness for OCP hardware. Version two for Hyperscale adds requirements for larger deployments. You do not need to complete version one first. Agree the route and use the current form. Separately, the Open Data Center for AI strategic initiative has developed a facility specification. Its guidance could inform a future OCP Ready for AI self-assessment, but whether and how that happens is still to be determined.

slides.title: What the self-assessment asks

cards.title: V1 · Delivery route
cards.body: Record clear height and width from the loading dock to goods-in.

cards.title: V1 · Rack power
cards.body: Record independent power feeds to the rack and maximum circuit capacity.

cards.title: V2 · Security
cards.body: Options include 24/7 checkpoint staffing, visitor pre-approval, government ID checks and escorts.

cards.title: V2 · Supplemental cooling
cards.body: If used, add notes and make technical analysis available on request. Rear-door heat exchangers are one example.

slides.transcript: The assessment records practical details. Version one asks for the delivery route’s clear height and width, independent rack power feeds, and circuit capacity. Version two includes round-the-clock checkpoint staffing and pre-approved, ID-checked, escorted visitors among its options. If supplemental cooling such as rear-door heat exchangers is used, add notes and make technical analysis available on request. These are examples, not the full checklist. The operator supplies the self-assessment, the Data Center Facility team reviews it, and the Foundation handles approval. This process does not include an OCP on-site audit.

slides.title: Read each recognition for what it covers

bullets.text: Confirm the edition and who performed the review.
Match it to the tenant’s actual needs.

slides.transcript: OCP Ready, Uptime Institute Tier certification, and TIA-942 certification have different purposes and review methods. Check the scope, edition, evaluator, and available evidence. A tenant may need several kinds of assurance. No single recognition answers every question about reliability, operation, or a particular deployment.

source_refs.basis: Single-module editorial revision; original teaching retained or consolidated.

slides.title: Nine areas support one facility
slides.transcript: Campus access and logistics get equipment to the site. Access controls protect it. Structure, power, and cooling support it. Telecommunications connects it. Operations and spares keep it running. Efficiency and certifications add evidence. These nine areas work together: a limit in one can constrain the whole deployment. Use the current assessment and actual site records, not appearances or general claims.

slides.title: From assessment to recognition
slides.transcript: The seven stages begin with the right assessment and a review of the evidence. Membership and program agreements follow, along with a presentation to the Data Center Facility community. Then come mark licensing and materials, Marketplace publication, and recognition with ongoing support. Agree the exact sequence with the Foundation. Completing the form is only the start.

slides.transcript: An OCP Ready facility must participate in the Solution Provider Program. Confirm membership, program agreements, and the certification mark license. Have authorized people complete them in the agreed order. Use the mark for the approved facility and scope. Tenants still need to check whether their equipment and plans fit the site.

slides.title: Keep the facility listing useful
slides.transcript: Prepare the name, description, images, company logo, specific link, and contact for the Marketplace. Include the site assessment and keep the claims consistent with approval. Keep this information current and discuss significant facility changes with the Foundation. Quarterly analytics, business-development conversations, and program support can help the ongoing relationship.

lms_catalog.short_description: Explore OCP Ready assessment paths, practical site questions, and the steps from evidence to facility recognition.
lms_catalog.overview: Understand how facility operators prepare evidence for OCP Ready recognition, and how project review and Foundation approval fit together. Explore the two established assessment paths and the journey to a public facility listing. This is a self-assessment and review process without an OCP on-site audit.
lms_catalog.duration_note: Includes narration, teaching videos, reading and the final two-question check. Optional exploration of the assessment spreadsheets, linked AI course and other resources takes additional time.

modules.summary: See how v1 records delivery height and width, independent rack power feeds and circuit capacity. Explore v2 options for 24/7 security staffing and visitors approved in advance, with ID checks and escorts. Learn about notes and technical analysis when added cooling, such as rear-door heat exchangers, is used. Follow the nine assessment areas through review, agreements and publication. A linked course explains the Open Data Center for AI initiative’s facility specification, which could inform a future OCP Ready for AI self-assessment. That possible assessment remains undecided.
